minutes_text:
Arts Commission

  Inglewood, California
  June 18, 2025

A meeting of the Inglewood Arts Commission was convened on June 18, 2025. Chairman
Jacques Lesure called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m., followed by the flag salute.

Ramara Rubin announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:
   Commissioner Aletha Metcalf - District 1
   Commissioner Olivia Alvitre - District 2
   Commissioner Phyllis Battle - District 3
   Commissioner Perryman-Banks - District 4
   Chairman Jacques Lesure - Commissioner at Large
  Absent:
   Commissioner Perryman-Banks - District 4

City Personnel present were as follows:

   Kerri Arroyo  Library Director
   Ramara Rubin  Secretary

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

MINUTES. Commissioner Metcalf moved, and Commissioner Battle seconded, that the
minutes for the Arts Commission meeting held on May 21, 2025 be approved.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Lesure, Perryman-Banks, and
Battle
Noes: None
   Arts Commission

  VERBAL REPORTS-Public Art‐Related Projects.
  a. Kerri Arroyo, Library Director, shared about the success of the Willie Stoffer
  Visual Artist Grant Exhibition highlighting the participation of Commissioner
  Battle and Metcalf and a special guest, Toni Morrison’s cousin Saundra.
  b. The City of Inglewood Main Library closed to the public on Saturday, June 14,
  2025, marking the beginning of the three-year renovation, and the Crenshaw
  Imperial-Branch will be the main hub for programming and services. Director
  Arroyo also shared an update on the Morningside Park Branch Library, noting
  that the building will be energized and refreshed, with cleanup efforts
  underway and the transfer of 7,000 books planned.
  c. The Senior Center will host a virtual visit with artist Tori Ellison, who will
  discuss her artwork Self Evident (for Sally Hemings). Director Arroyo
  provided an update on Helen Lundeberg’s The History of Transportation
  maintenance, the public art roster, and the development of the scope of
  practice for the public art consultant with the RFP expected to be released in
  the new fiscal year. Chairman Lesure noted the need to follow up on Michael
  Massenburg’s former artwork at the Forum.
  d. Director Arroyo reported an $81,000 increase in the public art fund balance
  and the pending transaction with the Creative House Gallery project, which
  includes reinstalling artwork on one utility box. Commissioner Battle inquired
  about public art funding.
  e. Chairman Lesure requested a detailed list of current public art related
  projects including pending and requisitioned. Commissioner Battle
  emphasized the need for a clear understanding of each project’s progress.

PUBLIC REMARKS.
  a. Helen Lessick thanked the Arts Commission, Creative House Gallery, and the
  Inglewood Public Library for supporting the Experiments in Public Art series.
  b. Jorge Gomez announces fundraiser for the Inglewood Night Market at Lalo’s Grill
  on July 19th, from 6 p.m. - 10 p.m.
  c. Commissioner Battle inquired about the budget allocation for the Night Market,
  seeking clarity on how funds are distributed to artists and performers.
  d. Joyce from Inglewood Open Studios expressed gratitude to the Inglewood Public
  Library for partnering in the success of the Willie Stoffer Artist Grant Exhibition
  and extended a public invitation to the upcoming IOS Mixer at Joan Robey’s
  studio.
   Arts Commission

COMMISSIONERS’ COMMENTS/INITIATIVES/ART CALENDAR.
  a. Helen Lessick encouraged the commission to review policies and procedures
  regarding the Percent for Art fund.
  b. Commissioner Battle inquired about Night Market funding in support of
  performing artists.
  c. Chairman Lesure noted his performance at the Los Angeles County Museum of
  Art’s Jazz at LACMA, the “Jacques Lesure Organ Quartet”.
  d. Commissioner Metcalf reported on her poetry reading at the Inglewood Senior
  Center in honor of Juneteenth.
  e. Commissioner Alvitre expressed appreciation to the public for attending the
  meeting and contributing their input and participation.

There being no further business to be presented, Chairman Lesure declared the meeting
adjourned at 7:22 p.m.
